description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Sony has announced the PS5 has crossed a major milestone: 100 million units sold since its November 2020 launch. This does not mean actually sold through to customers, but it's a good benchmark for how well the console is performing, sales-wise. The current reigning champ of console sales is the PS2 with more than 160 million sold, with the Nintendo Switch right behind it with around 157 million. In other sales news, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarins of Time remake for Switch 2 has sold an impressive 5 million in four days, making it the fastest-selling game on the Switch 2 so far. And finally, former Tekken boss Katsuhiro Harada had some harsh words for the Xbox Series S, calling it the "weaker child" of the Xbox Series family, and wishing it hadn't been released.
title: PlayStation 5 Crosses 100 Million Sold Milestone - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
Monster Hunter Outlanders reviewed by Hayes Madsen, played on iOS (iPhone 14 Plus), also available on Android.

"Monster Hunter Outlanders is simply one of those games that has too much stuff; it's overflowing with mobile-style fluff to keep track of, much of which gets in the way of enjoying that strong gameplay formula it clearly has. In many ways, it's genuinely remarkable how ambitious Outlanders is, and how deftly it manages to adapt the brilliance of Monster Hunter World into a smaller package. The smart streamlining of combat still keeps the intensity of hunts alive, while being more playable in short bursts. And while there's enough good here to keep you engaged, it equally comes with no shortage of frustrations in monetization, roadblocks, and the headache of endless menu management. That means, ultimately, Outlanders doesn't reach the heights of its console counterparts, but if you can go in with tempered expectations, the heart of Monster Hunter is still there."
title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Review

description:
Dive into the Southern Ocean as a research team, using the remotely operated vehicle SuBastian aboard the Schmidt Ocean Institute's research vessel Falkor (too), discovers the most southerly deep-sea hydrothermal vent on the planet and its habitat in this clip from Nat Geo's Expedition: Saving Our Seas, an upcoming documentary narrated by Ocean Conservationist Auliʻi Cravalho (‘Moana’). Nat Geo's Expedition: Saving Our Seas premieres November 13, at 9 p.m. EST on National Geographic and streams the next day on Disney+ and Hulu.

Observing the Ocean’s depths nearly 13,000 feet below the surface through the remotely operated vehicle SuBastian aboard the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s research vessel Falkor (too), a cohort of Explorers in the Southern Ocean, including oceanographer Dr. Andrew Thurber, biological oceanographer Dr. Kim Bernard and microbial oceanographer Dr. Allison Fong, surveys the basin’s depths and its icy surface in this clip.

Expedition: Saving Our Seas is a one-hour doc
title: Nat Geo's Expedition: Saving Our Seas - Official 'Southern Ocean - Hydrothermal Vent' Clip

description:
In Season 3’s first four episodes, The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power smartly gets back to basics. Although not big on epic fight scenes, the real attraction here is the series recalibrating itself, streamlining its plotlines and reminding us that this is, like the original Peter Jackson film trilogy, a simple but compelling story about good needing to triumph over evil. All the show’s most necessary players are back on the board with renewed vigor in what’s a clear attempt at bringing in new viewers to the Prime Video series, while hopefully not alienating those who have stuck with the show thus far.

Episodes 1-4 are available on Prime Video now, with Episodes 5 and 6 debuting on Nov. 18, and Episodes 7 and 8 finishing out the season on Nov. 25.

#IGN
title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-4 Review
